subject: Private GPU pool sizing & scaling playbook for Acme Analytics

Cc: EdgeCompute Corp <pm@edgecompute.com>

Subject: Private GPU pool: initial numbers and constraints

Hi Marissa / Grace —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The exec team is aligned on moving forward with a private deployment (VPC) for our inference workloads but we need a concrete sizing & scaling plan to share with procurement and our cloud partner. A few quick facts from our side: 

- Peak concurrent QPS (inference requests): expected 1,200 qps (short bursts, ~1–3 min), typical sustained 450 qps during business hours.
- Average request size: 520 tokens input, 80 tokens generated.
- 99th pct latency target: 300ms for LLM responses (us-west).
- Retention/compliance: logs must be retained for 180 days in our VPC.

Attached is a CSV with the per-endpoint expected qps/traffic breakdown. We need your recommended GPU pool config (node types, gpus per node), autoscaling policy, and a short runbook for network/VPC considerations (subnet sizing, NACLs, egress to S3).

Can the team turn around a draft by EOD Wednesday? Procurement will want initial TCO ballpark and any requirements for on-prem or single-tenant hosts.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Stein
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the clear numbers. We can deliver a draft sizing + runbook by Wednesday EOD. Quick clarifying Qs to make the sizing less conservative: 

- Are the 1,200 qps bursts multi-user (many concurrent small sessions) or a few heavy sessions?
- Expected model(s) to serve: are you targeting Llama-3-70B (unquantized) or a quantized 70B variant? This materially affects memory/KV cache.
- Do you have an upper bound on allowed GPU count per cluster (procurement limit)?

We'll propose a two-tier pool: primary low-latency nodes optimized for 99p SLAs and a cheaper burst pool for lower-cost quantized variants. Draft TCO will include reserved vs. on-demand mixes.

Marissa Cole
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Folks —

Based on the token sizes and 450 sustained qps / 1,200 burst, rough engineering rules of thumb:

- For an unquantized 70B model: ~80–96GB GPU memory required per replica; recommend A100 80GB or H100 80GB equivalent. Memory/kv cache pushes effective footprint up.
- For a quantized 70B (4-bit): ~20–30GB effective memory; can run on 48–80GB cards depending on seq len and batching.
- Latency headroom: allocate ~20–30% spare capacity for 99p SLA headroom and autoscaler cooldowns.

Preliminary node suggestion (primary pool):
- 8x H100-80GB (per node) instances running RW runtime in low-latency mode, each node serving ~150–200 qps steady depending on batching.
- Burst pool: 12x A100-80GB with quantized model variants; cheaper fallback for non-critical workloads.

Autoscaling: prefer target-based scaling on token throughput + burst capacity buffer that can be pre-warmed via warm-standby nodes in the VPC. Set cooldowns short for burst windows but use predictive scaling tied to the traffic schedule Rachel provided.

I'll put numbers into a spreadsheet and include a preliminary TCO.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Dev / Marissa —

Answers inline: 
- Bursts are multi-tenant: traffic comes from many user sessions (dashboard refreshes) rather than a few long-running chats. Expect 1,200 qps to persist for up to 3–4 minutes during major business events.
- Model plan: start with a quantized 70B variant (fast path) and a pinned unquantized 70B for a small percentage of requests that need highest fidelity (approx 5–10%).
- Procurement hard limit: prefer to stay under 40 physical GPUs for first phase (budgetary).

Given that, please size assuming a hard cap of 40 GPUs in phase 1 and include an option to expand to 80 GPUs in phase 2. Also include network egress considerations to S3: we run logs to our S3 in the same VPC/region and need NAT/GW throughput to be provisioned.

Thanks — will aim to circulate to procurement after your draft.

Rachel

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: network & VPC checklist

Quick VPC/network notes for procurement and Acme's cloud partner: 

- Subnets: carve out dedicated private subnets for GPU nodes with /22 to start (allows ~1k IPs; simplifies node replacement).
- NAT/Gateway: ensure egress bandwidth >= 5 Gbps per 10 GPU nodes (monitor; can increase). Use gateway endpoints to S3 where possible to avoid NAT bottlenecks.
- NACLs/SGs: restrict control-plane ports to Redwood control plane IP ranges and Acme ops CIDR; open only required ports for health checks and KV sync.
- Storage: use local NVMe for model weights caching with periodic snapshot to EBS/S3. Ensure IOPS baseline supports ~200MB/s sustained per node during model load.
- Monitoring: span VPC flow logs to log bucket in Acme account; provide log retention configuration as part of the runbook.

I'll attach the updated private architecture diagram with recommended subnet/CIDR ranges and the runbook steps.

- Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Network & Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

Commercial notes for procurement:

- SLA: 99.5% uptime on primary pool; credits scale with downtime. For 99p latency guarantees we need a short run-in period (2 weeks) to tune batching & cache; we'll include that in onboarding.

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: sizing & scaling playbook for Acme Analytics — draft deliverable

Team / Rachel —

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is the draft playbook and sizing spreadsheet; high level summary below: 

- Phase 1 (<=40 GPUs): Primary pool = 16 H100-80GB nodes (1 GPU per node assumed in private config) tuned for low-latency with RW runtime; supports ~10–14 qps per GPU for the unquantized 70B 99p SLA slice and ~25–30 qps per GPU for the quantized variant. Burst pool = 24 A100-80GB nodes running quantized 70B fallback. Expected effective throughput under phase 1: sustained ~450 qps with 1,200 qps bursts covered via pre-warmed burst pool within procurement cap.
- Autoscaling policy: target token throughput with headroom=30%. Warm-standby nodes (4 GPUs) reserved and pre-warm hooks for predictable events. Scale-up cooldowns short (30s); scale-down cooldowns longer (5m) to avoid oscillation.
- Network/runbook: use /22 private subnets, gateway endpoints to S3, NAT throughput baseline 10 Gbps for phase 1, healthcheck ports and SGs as Hiro outlined.
- TCO: included reserved vs. on-demand options; ballpark monthly run-rate attached (see spreadsheet).

Next steps: 
1) Grace to send MA + TCO summary to procurement (Grace: will you sync with Acme procurement?).
2) EdgeCompute to confirm host limits and any single-tenant constraints (cc'd EdgeCompute PM).
3) Redwood infra to prepare onboarding run (2-week tuning window) and sample logs configuration.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up with Rachel + Procurement + EdgeCompute for Fri to finalize MA items. Feedback welcome and we'll iterate before procurement submission.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
